findings_addressed.oracle: Two independent oracles: (1) manager.store.load() round-trip checks all injected fields (name, provider, model, notes, tags) — not just id; (2) a direct sqlite3.connect() query on the raw sessions table verifies the provider, name, model, and notes columns contain the exact serialised values, bypassing the ORM layer entirely.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/session.py SessionStore._save_session_transaction(), replace `session.provider.value` with `"openai"` in the INSERT VALUES tuple. The raw SQL oracle `SELECT provider FROM sessions WHERE id=?` returns `"openai"` instead of `"anthropic"`, failing `assert raw_provider == ProviderName.ANTHROPIC.value`.
findings_addressed.weakness_eliminated: Previously only asserted `loaded is not None` and `loaded.id == session.id`, which would pass even if the provider field was silently corrupted to a hardcoded default. Now asserts every injected field via the ORM layer AND independently via raw SQL, making the test falsifiable under any field-level serialization defect.

notes: Hardened test_session_manager_requires_session_store_type to verify all injected fields (name, provider, model, notes, tags) survive the round-trip via manager.store.save/load, plus an independent sqlite3.connect() raw SQL oracle on the sessions table to catch provider/field serialization errors that the ORM layer would mask. The test is now distinct from TestSessionDataIntegrity.test_session_roundtrip: it verifies the SessionManager.store reference is wired to the real backend (not a stub) while also providing stronger field-coverage assertions.
